newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shrs seen higher in Hindu new year this wk.
newsitem.headline: Indian shrs seen higher in Hindu new year this wk.

text.p: Indian stocks are seen marginally better in slow trade next week helped by a market correction after a recent slide, brokers and analysts said at the weekend.
But volumes would be light because of vacationing players, they said.
Most markets open briefly for an auspicious "moorat" session on Sunday evening to herald the Hindu New Year, but normal trading on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) will resume only on Wednesday.
"We hope to start the new year on a better note," said Zubin Tampal, dealer at Bombay broker Motilal Oswal. "The year that went by was a dismal one."
The top-30 BSE index dropped 81.91 points, or 2.60 percent, to 3,066.66 in the week to Thursday, after falling 102.09 points the previous week. The exchange was closed on Friday for a local holiday.
A reversal of fortune will most likely come from a technical correction after the market buckled under relentless speculative selling following government action against tobacco conglomerate ITC Ltd.
ITC's shares fell sharply after a federal agency swooped down on the firm on October 30 and detained top officials.
It fell on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) by 77.25 rupees, or 24.6 percent, to 244 between October 30 and November 6, before recovering to end the week at 253 rupees.
The government arrested several senior ITC officials including two former chairmen for allegedly violating India's foreign exchange laws.
Analysts said the fall in ITC shares set off a chain reaction, dragging prices down across the board and driving wary investors further away.
The selling was largely speculation-driven as reflected by the backwardation charges the share attracted at the close of the BSE's weekly account.
Backwardation is a charge on short sellers to carry-forward transactions from one settlement to another. It reflects large oversold positions.

Brokers expect players to square their positions ahead of ITC's board meeting on November 15, when Indian finance firms and Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc which together hold 70 percent of ITC equity, review the working.
"I'm looking at slight improvement," said Rasesh Maniar, dealer at Mukesh Babu Financial Services Ltd. "But some traders think it will go down."
He said the total absence of retail investors and redemption demand on domestic funds was expected to stall a rally from gaining momentum.
The recent fall in prices at home against rises in global depositary receipts listed abroad offer arbitrage opportunities to foreign funds, he said.
